text: When a young man is of such excellence as to have made a name for himself by some signal achievement, it were much to the detriment of his city were it unable at once to make use of him, but had to wait until he had grown old, and had lost, with youth, that alacrity and vigour by which his country might have profited.
author: Niccolo Machiavelli
reference: Discourses on the First Decade of Titus Livius
